newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks close higher as tech shares surge.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks close higher as tech shares surge.

text.p: Wall Street stocks finished the week on a positive note, staging a broad rally on Friday that was paced by stirring gains in the computer group.
The Dow industrials climbed 35 points to close unofficially at 7922. Hewlett-Packard Co led the blue chips higher, gaining 2-7/8 to 61-3/16.

Other computer makers also showed solid gains, lifting the Nasdaq Composite by nearly 12 points to about 1503. It was the seventh consecutive record for the index and its first close above the 1500 level.

Analysts said several factors fueled the advance by computer shares. One of them was strong quarterly earnings announced by Compaq Computer Corp on Thursday. Investors appeared to seize on the news as a favorable sign for the entire group.
Shares in Compaq jumped 3-3/4 to 123-7/8, and Dell Computer Corp surged 9-3/8 to 138.

"People have had the jitters for second-quarter technology numbers and then Compaq comes in," said Daniel Kunstler, a J.P Morgan analyst. "What's going on is an interpretation that what's going on with Compaq has got to be good for Dell too."
Earnings-related news dominated the action among individual issues. Crown Cork & Seal Co slid 6-7/16 to 49-15/16 after the company released second-quarter results that fell short of estimates.

MCI Communications Corp tumbled 7-3/8 to 35 after warning its earnings for this and next year would likely fall short of Wall Street estimates. The company blamed delays in gaining access to U.S. local phone service markets.
The deal cast doubt on whether MCI's planned acquisition by British Telecom Plc would occur on the terms originally set.
